title: Card transactions with fraud flags, September

findings.headline: Fraud is concentrated in night-time transactions
findings.detail: Night (0–5) has a fraud rate of 30.8% across 718 transactions, against 0.3% to 0.7% in the other time bands. Night is only 7% of volume.

findings.headline: Fraud rate is very high in AE and SG
findings.detail: AE has a fraud rate of 28.6% (206 rows) and SG 31% (187 rows), against 1.6% for IN. These two countries are just 3.8% of rows (2% + 1.8%).

findings.headline: Digital goods and online show high fraud rates
findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% fraud rate (1,130 rows) against 0.3% to 0.7% elsewhere. Online is 6.3% against 0.3% for Contactless and 0.5% for Chip.

findings.headline: Fraud rose sharply from early September
findings.detail: The weekly fraud rate went from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 4.0% and 4.1% in the weeks of 14 and 21 Sep. The last week is partial (727 rows) and shows 1.8%.

findings.headline: Small transactions have the highest fraud rate
findings.detail: The lowest amount band (1.71 to 535.9) has an 11.4% fraud rate, against 0.3% to 0.6% in the higher bands. Low-value testing of cards is one possible pattern to check.

next_steps: Check whether the night, AE/SG, digital goods and small-amount fraud cases overlap, by cross-tabulating the 272 fraud rows on these factors.
Review the 14 and 21 Sep weeks to see which cards and merchants drove the rise, and whether it continued after 28 Sep.
Test tighter rules or step-up checks on night-time online digital goods purchases abroad, and measure the false alarms they create.

findings.detail: AE has a fraud rate of 28.6% (206 rows) and SG 31% (187 rows), against 1.6% for IN. US (0.7%) and GB (0.8%) are low. AE and SG together are 3.8% of rows (2% + 1.8%).

findings.detail: Digital goods has a 20.4% fraud rate (1,130 rows) against 0.3% to 0.7% in every other category. Online is 6.3% against 0.3% for Contactless and 0.5% for Chip.

findings.headline: Weekly fraud rate peaked mid-September, then fell
findings.detail: The weekly fraud rate went from 0.6% (week of 31 Aug) to 1.7%, then 4.0% and 4.1% in the weeks of 14 and 21 Sep. The last week is partial (727 rows) and shows 1.8%.

next_steps: Cross-tabulate the 272 fraud rows by hour band, country, category, channel and amount band to see how much the patterns overlap.
Compare the weeks of 14 and 21 Sep with the weeks either side, by hour, country and category, to see what changed.
Trial step-up checks on night-time online digital goods purchases from AE and SG, and count the genuine customers they stop.
conclusion: Fraud is not spread evenly. It is far higher at night (30.8%), in AE and SG (28.6% and 31%), in digital goods (20.4%), online (6.3%) and small amounts (11.4%). First, find out how these patterns overlap among the 272 fraud rows, so rules target the right group.
limits: This review uses summary figures only, so it cannot show why fraud is higher in these groups, how the patterns overlap, or whether the flags are accurate.
